# SasaVenos Says Phase Potentiation Allows Using A Hold Phase To Build Base For Front Lever Pull-Up

SasaVenos says that if you struggle with learning a front lever pull-up, you can have a phase of training where you only work on holds to build up your base and muscle size, and then after a month or two focus solely on training the front lever pull-up with higher volumes. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Details

- If you really struggle with learning a front lever pull-up, you can have a different phase of training where you will only work on holds to build up your base while also working on building some muscle size in your rear delts and mid traps. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- After you are done with this phase, a month or two, you can focus solely on training your front lever pull-up with higher volumes. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]
- You have a stronger base and more muscle in areas you need, making the job much easier because you phase-potentiated your goals. [src: vid-BBuB0XMVhDw]

## Evidence

- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "if you really struggle with learning a front lever pull-up, you can have a different phase of training where you will only work on holds or presses or raises, however you like to call them, to build up your base while also working on building some muscle size in your rear delts and mid traps."
- vid-BBuB0XMVhDw (SasaVenos): "After you're done with this phase of training, a month or two, you can focus solely on training your front lever pull-up with higher volumes."
